newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA H1 UNEMPLOYMENT RATE RISES TO 12.1 PCT.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA H1 UNEMPLOYMENT RATE RISES TO 12.1 PCT.

text.p: Venezuela's unemployment rate rose to 12.1 percent in the first half of 1997 compared to 11.1 percent in the same period last year, a top government official said Tuesday.

The average unemployment rate over the first half of the year was down from 12.6 percent in the first quarter, Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI) Director Miguel Bolivar told a news conference.
The unemployment rate stood at 12.4 percent at the end of 1996 and peaked at over 13 percent in January.
The government has set a target of reducing the jobless rate by two percentage points this year.
The current unemployment rate is equivalent to 1.109 million people from a labor force of 9.187 million, Bolivar said.
Of the total labor force, 48.7 percent belongs to the informal sector, down from 49.4 percent in the first half of 1996, he said.
The OCEI's broad definition of informal activities includes all businesses with five or fewer employees.
Venezuela's total population currently stands at 22.611 million, according to OCEI figures.
